name: The romance in four phases
hint: Two who meet, fall, pull back and fight for love. The ending is happy. Each step can become several chapters.

parts.title: The meeting
chapters: The first
(ca 1 %) One lead in their life: what they want, what is missing and the lie about love they live by. Give the reader a reason to like them at once.
The second
(ca 3 %) The other lead, with a goal of their own and a reason not to want to fall in love right now. In dual POV, this is their first chapter.
The meeting
(ca 8-10 %) They meet in a way that grates or sparks, and the reader knows at once that these two are the couple.
Not a chance
(ca 15 %) Both give concrete reasons why this can never become anything. The reasons must hold for half the book.
Bound together
(ca 20-25 %) Something outside forces them to keep meeting: a job, an inheritance, a bet, a fake relationship. Without it, they just go home.

parts.title: Falling in love
chapters: A first sign
(ca 30 %) A look, a laugh or a favour that will not be forgotten. One of them admits to themselves that something has happened.
Beneath the surface
(ca 38 %) They see each other as they are: a vulnerability is shown and received. The outer obstacle starts to shrink.
Maybe after all
(ca 45 %) They let themselves hope. The first real closeness, with a clear yes from both.
The midpoint
(ca 50 %) The kiss, the night or the confession. It seems to hold, but the inner wound is still untouched.

parts.title: The retreat
chapters: The doubt
(ca 58 %) The old wound makes itself felt, often through something outside: an ex, an offer, a glimpse of a secret.
The wall
(ca 66 %) One pulls back to stay safe, and the other feels it. The lie about love takes over.
The break-up
(ca 75 %) It ends, about three quarters of the way in, for a reason rooted in both their wounds. The reader should understand both and still want to shake them.

parts.title: Fighting for love
chapters: The dark night
(ca 82 %) Life without the other, and what it costs. The side characters say what the leads do not want to hear.
The realisation
(ca 88 %) Each sees their lie and understands what has to change, inside and not just on the surface.
The grand gesture
(ca 93 %) Someone risks everything, in a way that heals exactly the wound the book showed at the start. Often both need to act, and whoever did the hurting truly apologises.
Happy ending
(ca 98 %) Love as it looks when it holds, shown in a scene. Ideally a final image that echoes the first chapter.

name: Feel-good and romantic comedy
hint: A new start, a meeting that grates, warmth, a setback and a warm ending. The lead's new life carries as much as the love story.

parts.title: The new start
chapters: A life in flux
(ca 3 %) Something ends: a job, a relationship, a city. Show the humour and the voice from the first line.
The place
(ca 10 %) A town, a shop or a house to land in. Make it both charming and difficult, so there is something to win.
The meeting
(ca 15 %) Two who should not fit together at all collide, ideally in a funny way. The reader sees the couple before they do.

parts.title: The warmth
chapters: The community
(ca 25 %) The people around them step forward, each with a quirk. The lead starts, reluctantly, to belong.
The project
(ca 35 %) A shared goal, saving the café or putting on the festival, forces the couple to work together.
Closer
(ca 45 %) It grates less and less. An honest talk, a shared laugh, a first kiss.
The good moment
(ca 55 %) Everything seems possible: the place thrives and love holds. The warmest chapter in the book.

parts.title: The setback
chapters: The past comes back
(ca 65 %) An ex, an offer from back home or a secret. The lead's old life pulls at them.
The threat
(ca 72 %) The place is at stake: it may be sold, closed or torn down. Love and the place are threatened by the same thing.
Apart
(ca 80 %) It looks like it is over, between them and for the place. The lead packs a bag.

parts.title: Home
chapters: The community rallies
(ca 88 %) The people around step up, and someone dares to say what needs saying.
The choice
(ca 93 %) The lead chooses the place and love, with a gesture that shows they have changed. The love interest shows they have changed too.
The warm ending
(ca 98 %) Life as it turned out, better than the plan. A celebration, a new season and hope for what comes next.
